summary: Initial POC scoping between Redwood AE/SE and Solstice Health to decide between hosted, dedicated, or private deployment. Key topics: success criteria (latency < 200ms 95p, throughput 200 QPS, cost targets), workload sizing (avg token lengths, QPS, KV cache needs), security/compliance constraints (SOC2, SSO, KMS, data residency), benchmark plan and timeline (benchmark next week, 2-week POC), and next steps for pricing and docs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Karen Liu (Solstice), Arjun Mehta (Solstice), Sofia Ramirez (Solstice)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time today, quick intros?
[00:12] Dr. Karen Liu: Karen here, head of ML at Solstice, we run a patient triage assistant and some summarization pipelines, mostly sensitive PHI-like data, so compliance is big for us.
[00:27] Arjun Mehta: Arjun, infra, I look after cloud networking and infra decisions.
[00:32] Sofia Ramirez: Sofia, compliance - mainly SOC2 stuff, encryption and audit logs.
[00:40] Maya Patel: Great. Liam from our side?
[00:44] Liam Chen: Hey all, Liam Chen, solutions engineer, I'll dig into perf and benchmarking with you.
[00:48] Maya Patel: Cool. Goal today is to scope a POC, align on success criteria, sizing, benchmarks and timeline, and help you pick hosted vs dedicated vs private.

[01:05] Dr. Karen Liu: High level constraints: latency matters for chat (patient-facing) - we want 95th percentile below 200ms for prefix length ~50 tokens. For backend batch summarization latency is less critical but throughput and cost matter. Also we can't send raw PHI off-prem without extra controls.
[01:35] Liam Chen: Understood. Rough question: what's your expected QPS for the chat path?
[01:40] Arjun Mehta: Peak is about 200 QPS during business hours, avg about 40 QPS; typical request ~120 tokens in/out combined.
[01:50] Maya Patel: Good, that helps. For 200 QPS we usually recommend dedicated pools to hit consistent latency; hosted can work if you accept auto-scaling variability and possible multi-tenant limits.

[02:10] Sofia Ramirez: On compliance - we need SOC2, SSO via SAML, audit logs for all requests and KMS integration for keys. Also data residency - EU region is preferred.
[02:25] Maya Patel: We can provide SOC2 docs, SAML SSO, audit logs export, and edge of VPC/private control plane for our Private offering. KMS/HSM integrations are supported on Dedicated & Private. Hosted supports customer-managed keys via BYOK in some cases, we can share details.

[03:00] Liam Chen: To pick between modes: hosted = fastest to get started + lower ops, but less isolation; dedicated = reserved GPU capacity, predictable single-tenant performance and easier KMS; private = full control (VPC/private control plane / on-prem) but longer lead time and higher cost.

[03:30] Dr. Karen Liu: What about cost numbers rough? Ballpark per-token vs committed capacity?
[03:36] Maya Patel: Roughly for hosted generative we price per-token; dedicated is monthly commit by GPU units (sustained throughput) - for your 200 QPS chat, you'll likely need a 6-8 GPU pool depending on model selection and quantization. We'll send a cost spreadsheet.

[04:00] Arjun Mehta: How do you handle KV cache / long-conversation state? We have threads that can go 4-5 turns, users expect snappy replies.
[04:12] Liam Chen: We have prefix/KV caching and continuous batching; for chat we can keep model KV cache hot which reduces per-token latency. Dedicated gives more cache hit predictability. Hosted tries to cache but eviction is possible in multi-tenant scenarios.

[04:40] Sofia Ramirez: On the PHI question - we likely need a Private deployment for production, but for the POC maybe dedicated in a private VPC is acceptable?
[04:52] Maya Patel: That's a common path - POC on Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS, then migrate to Private/on-prem for full data isolation if needed.

[05:10] Dr. Karen Liu: Success criteria suggestion: chat 95p latency <200ms for 50-token prefix at 200 QPS sustained for 15 min window; summarization cost < $0.002 per 1k tokens processed (example target); model quality equal or better than baseline (our current model) on 5 eval prompts. Also security checklist passed.
[05:40] Liam Chen: Good checklist. We'll design benchmark tests: synthetic replay of 1 hour of traffic at your profile, and a smaller sample of real anonymized transcripts for quality eval.

[06:05] Arjun Mehta: For benchmarking, we need to know network egress patterns and VPC setup. Can we run inside our VPC?
[06:15] Maya Patel: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private networking; for hosted we can accept traffic from your VPC via secure endpoints and IP allowlists but not full peering. Private is fully inside your network. We'll detail options in the doc.

[06:40] Dr. Karen Liu: Timeline? We want to decide within 4 weeks and run a 2-week POC right after.
[06:48] Maya Patel: Proposed timeline: this week finalize scope & pricing; week of 3/8 run benchmarks; week of 3/15 start 2-week POC; decision by 3/29. Is that aligned?
[06:58] Arjun Mehta: That works if we can get benchmark tooling and sample payloads fast.

[07:10] Liam Chen: I'll prepare a benchmark plan with scripts, payload formats, expected metrics, and guidance on running both hosted and dedicated tests. We recommend measuring latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, token cost, and cache hit rates.

[07:30] Sofia Ramirez: On audit logs retention and access controls - we need logs for 1 year and RBAC so only a few folks can access them.
[07:40] Maya Patel: We have log export to your S3, and RBAC in Redwood Console with roles. Retention options we'll cover. For Private we can keep logs entirely in your environment.

[08:00] Dr. Karen Liu: Model selection - we use a Llama-variant today, are you supporting open models? Do you do quantization?
[08:12] Liam Chen: We support a catalog of open models and provide quantized variants; we also recommend quantization to reduce GPU needs. We'll suggest model + quantization profiles based on your latency/quality tradeoff.

[08:35] Arjun Mehta: For the dedicated sizing, you mentioned 6-8 GPUs. What instance types?
[08:42] Maya Patel: Depends on model; for 4-bit quantized Llama-like models we often recommend A10G or H100 depending on sequence length. We'll size precisely after we see your token distribution.

[09:05] Dr. Karen Liu: What about fallback policies if dedicated capacity is saturated? We need graceful degradation.
[09:12] Liam Chen: Redwood supports smart routing and fallback to hosted tier or smaller model variants automatically based on policy. We'll configure canary and fallback policies in the POC.

[09:30] Arjun Mehta: Is there a way to test Private without full on-prem setup?
[09:36] Maya Patel: We can do a private-like test using a private control plane in your cloud region, or a short-term dedicated private deployment in our lab to validate networking and KMS integration. That takes more lead time.

[10:00] Sofia Ramirez: For encryption, we need to ensure KMS envelopes and HSM-backed keys are supported for private. Also need clarity on data-at-rest encryption for logs and model caches.
[10:12] Liam Chen: Yes, HSM-backed KMS is supported on Dedicated & Private; logs and caches are encrypted at rest and we can provide the encryption configuration in the security pack.

[10:30] Dr. Karen Liu: Regarding quality evals, we'll provide 200 representative prompts and expected outputs for scoring.
[10:38] Maya Patel: Perfect - we'll run automated evals and human review for edge cases. We'll also set up regression alerts in Redwood Optimize.

[11:00] Liam Chen: Quick notes on metrics we'll collect in the benchmark: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit ratio, hardware utilization, error rates, cold-start latency.

[11:20] Arjun Mehta: For the POC acceptance criteria - if hosted meets latency but fails on compliance we still might accept hosted for internal pilot but require dedicated/private for prod.
[11:32] Maya Patel: That's a reasonable plan; we often do a two-stage approach: hosted for dev/exploration, dedicated for security-sensitive POC, then private for production if required.

[11:50] Dr. Karen Liu: Any blockers? We need to check procurement for a committed capacity if we choose dedicated, and legal will need the SOC2 + DPA before sending any PHI-like data.
[12:05] Sofia Ramirez: Also want to see endpoint-level audit samples and access logs format.
[12:12] Maya Patel: We'll attach sample audit logs and DPA; I'll route those after the call.

[12:30] Maya Patel: Recap / next steps - Maya to send pricing and security docs; Liam to send benchmark plan and scripts; Arjun to share traffic profile and anonymized sample transcripts; Solstice to confirm timeline.
[12:48] Dr. Karen Liu: Ok we'll aim to have profile and transcripts by 3/07.
[12:53] Arjun Mehta: I'll get those.
[12:55] Maya Patel: Great. Anything else?
[13:00] Sofia Ramirez: No, thanks.
[13:05] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials.

End of transcript
